drawing_callouts.rule: A placement is validated when its own callout on the factory location drawing (each callout paired with at most one placement of its label, nearest first) lands within 0.07 normalized of it under two least-squares fits of that page: one on independently read controls (jet-bumper caps and flipper pivots, or another crisp mechanism feature where balloons hide a pivot), and one, measured leave-one-out, on the page's other callout reads, from which any read beyond the limit is dropped. Placements without such a read keep their table status. Placements measured on a drawing are never checked against it.

method.artwork_caveat: The VPW table identifies itself as 'Lord Of The Rings - Valinor Edition' with original artwork, so where its insert layout departs from the printed diagrams that is an artwork difference, not an error. Its 19-LED pattern matches the factory one but sits 0.100 further back.

28.reason: The 2022 vector DR.4 prints box 28 on the middle of the Balrog arm, 0.022 normalized from Hanibal's script-bound sw28 and 0.089 from JPSalas', which sits at the arm's pivot end; VPW binds no sw28 object. The switch is inside the Balrog assembly behind the front hit plate.

41.reason: All three tables agree on y and spread x from 0.182 to 0.266; the 2022 vector DR.4 prints box 41 0.004 normalized from VPW's script-bound sw41, so VPW's measurement is published instead of the per-axis median.

method.rule: Every located placement is validated in exactly one of four ways, listed per placement under validation_basis: all three factory-layout recreations agree within the threshold; a table object's own factory callout confirms it (drawing_callouts, 0.07 normalized under both fits); a projection onto the mechanism a coil drives is confirmed by the factory bottom view drawing that coil's assembly beside it; or the device is measured on the factory drawing that draws it, through that page's control fit.
method.why_all_three: Independence between the three recreations is unestablished and the two available signals disagree. Measured: the JPSalas and Hanibal tables agree with each other to within 0.0155 on every lamp both model, while either differs from VPW by up to 0.187. Documented: VPW credits an 'EBIsLit - Baseline playfield scan' and JPSalas records its playfield as 'based on Ebislit's playfield', while Hanibal declares only "4k Mod" in its title and names no baseline. Requiring all three for table agreement alone removes the need to guess which signal describes the lineage; anything less needs a factory drawing.

projections.reason: The trough's dual opto transmitter and receiver boards (515-0173-00 / 515-0174-00) carry both the eject beam (14) and the stacking beam (15), and PDF 123 labels both boards S14 and S15; the stacking beam sits above the eject beam, so in plan it shares switch 14's position.
